description: Caller claims to be from Microsoft, Apple, Google, or other tech company reporting computer virus or security issue
indicators: claiming computer has virus or malware
asking for payment for tech support services
using technical jargon to confuse victim
creating sense of urgency about computer security
claiming to be from Microsoft, Apple, Google, or Windows
requesting credit card or banking information
threatening data loss or identity theft
example_scripts: This is Microsoft tech support. We detected a virus on your computer and need remote access to fix it.
Your computer is sending us error messages. We need to connect remotely to resolve the issue.
We've detected suspicious activity on your Windows license. Pay $299 for our protection service.
This is Apple security. Your iCloud account has been compromised. We need to verify your information.
Your computer has been infected with a dangerous virus. Allow us remote access immediately to prevent data loss.
We're calling from Windows technical department. Your computer is at risk and needs immediate attention.
Your antivirus subscription has expired. Renew now for $399 or your computer will be vulnerable.
We detected illegal activity from your IP address. Pay $500 to avoid legal action and secure your system.
This is Google support. Your account will be suspended unless you verify your payment information now.
Your computer is part of a botnet. We need to install our security software immediately.
red_flags: Legitimate tech companies don't request remote access unsolicited
Real tech support doesn't demand immediate payment
Companies don't detect viruses on your computer remotely
Legitimate services don't require gift card payments
Real tech support provides verifiable contact information
